name: Flex

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.code:
<Flex gap="2">
  <Box>One</Box>
  <Box>Two, with more to say than the first</Box>
</Flex>

examples.title: A Fixed Side and a Growing One
examples.code:
Account Profile Billing

The side keeps its width, and this part grows into the rest.

examples.title: Wrapping
examples.code:
<Flex flexWrap="wrap" columnGap="3" rowGap="1">
  {Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) => (
    <Button key={i} size="small">
      Item {i + 1}
    </Button>
  ))}
</Flex>

accessibility:
- **No role of its own:** a Flex adds nothing to the accessibility tree, apart from `role="list"`
  on a `ul` or `ol`, which Safari otherwise drops once Bulma's reset hides the markers.
- **Reversed directions:** `row-reverse` and `column-reverse` change what's seen and not the
  reading or Tab order, so what's seen and what's read can disagree (WCAG 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence
  and 2.4.3 Focus Order). Use them only where the order doesn't carry meaning, or put the children
  in the order you want them read.
- **Landmarks:** with `as="nav"`, `"aside"`, `"section"` or `"main"`, the Flex is the landmark. A
  `section` is a region only once it has a name.
summary: The `Flex` component is a flex container with CSS's own defaults, taking the flex container's properties as props. It's a row that doesn't wrap, with its children stretched across it and no gap, until you set otherwise. Use it for a layout of your own, such as a fixed side beside a growing one, with `flexGrow` and `flexShrink` on the children. Its children's own block margins are zeroed, so the gap is the only space. For a column of blocks or a row of controls with Bulma's spacing already in place, `Stack` and `Group` start closer.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render. With `ul` or `ol`, give it `li` children: it restates `role="list"`, which Bulma's list reset takes away in Safari.

props.name: flexDirection
props.description: The main axis, a row unless set. `row-reverse` and `column-reverse` change only what's seen: reading and Tab order still follow the children's order (WCAG 1.3.2 and 2.4.3).

props.name: flexWrap
props.description: Whether children move to a new line when they don't fit. Unset, CSS's own `nowrap`.

props.name: alignItems
props.description: How each child sits across the main axis. Unset, CSS's own `stretch`.

props.name: justifyContent
props.description: Where the children sit along the main axis.

props.name: alignContent
props.description: How wrapped lines share the space across the main axis.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between children, a step of Bulma's gap scale. None by default.

props.name: rowGap
props.description: Space between wrapped lines, when it differs from `gap`.

props.name: columnGap
props.description: Space between children along a row, when it differs from `gap`.

props.name: children
props.description: What it lays out. The margins Bulma gives them are zeroed, the bottom one in a Stack and the top and bottom in the others, so `gap` is the only space between them. A `Columns` child keeps its own top and side margins, and takes at the bottom the one Bulma gives the last Columns in a container, the column gap pulled back in (none when gapless), so its columns line up.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the element `as` renders.

parts.catchAll: Remaining props of the element selected by as and Bulma helper props

types.name: BulmaGapStep
types.summary: A gap step as `gap`, `columnGap` and `rowGap` take it: a value from `validGaps`, or the same step written as a number (`gap={2}`, `gap={1.5}`). `Grid` took its gaps as numbers before the gap helpers were shared, so every gap prop still does.

types.name: LayoutElement
types.summary: The elements Stack, Group, Center and Flex can render as: Container's landmarks and sections, a list, a form or a fieldset.
